title: A Rapid and Reproducible Protocol for Protein Extraction from Actinomyces
author: Yalpi Karthik
materials: Figure 2. Diagrammatic representation of cell separation.

steps.title: Harvest culture pellet
steps.instruction: Retrieve the Actinomyces culture grown in SCN broth at an optical density of 0.6–0.8 (measured at 600 nm) after 8–10 days incubation at 30 ± 2 °C with shaking at 100 rpm; centrifuge the broth at 7 000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C to collect the cell pellet.

steps.title: Separate pellet from supernatant
steps.instruction: Transfer the supernatant (Tube B) to a fresh tube, decontaminate and discard it according to WHO biosafety hazardous guidelines; retain the cell pellet (Tube A) for further processing.

steps.title: Wash pellet
steps.instruction: Wash the pellet 2–3 times with 0.05 M PBS, pH 7.0 (free of chelating agents); after each wash resuspend the pellet in PBS and centrifuge at 7 000 rpm for 10 min at 4 °C, discarding the supernatant each time.

substeps.instruction: Add 0.05 M PBS (pH 7.0) to the pellet.
Discard supernatant and repeat 2–3 times total.

steps.title: Acetone treatment
steps.instruction: Discard the final wash supernatant, add 10 mL chilled acetone to the washed pellet, incubate for 15–30 min, then remove residual acetone by flushing the pellet with a stream of nitrogen gas.

steps.title: Extract proteins with SDS
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL of 1 % SDS solution to the acetone‑treated pellet, incubate for 2 min, then store the protein extract at –20 °C for short‑term use or lyophilize for long‑term storage.

steps.title: Quantify protein by Bradford
steps.instruction: Perform a Bradford assay using a BSA standard curve; measured absorbance at 595 nm is 0.495 (triplicate). Using the regression equation Abs = 0.0022 × [Protein] (µg/mL) + 0.001 (R² ≈ 0.999), calculate protein concentration ≈224 µg/mL. With an extract volume of 1 mL this corresponds to 0.224 mg protein, derived from 1 mg (0.001 g) dry cell weight, i.e., 224 mg protein per g dry weight.

substeps.instruction: Prepare Bradford reagent and BSA standards.
Measure absorbance of samples at 595 nm (triplicate).
Record final protein yield (224 mg g⁻¹ dry weight).
